We have applied first template 20810, got two products: product1 = "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1" and product2 = "O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F". The route must use templates in order: ['20810', '2895', '1914397', '1914398', '1914399', '74054'].

We have applied 20810, then 2895 on product1 gave nitro substitution? Actually 2895 applied to product1 gave "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1". Good.

Then 1914397 applied to that gave two fragments: "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCNCC1" and "O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2". So we have split into two molecules.

Now need to apply 1914398 to appropriate fragment. We applied to the aromatic nitro-bromo fused ring gave "BrBr" and "O=[N+]([O-])c1ccc2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2". That seems odd: product includes BrBr (bromine dimer) and a modified aromatic. Probably template 1914398 is a dehalogenation? It gave BrBr as leaving group.

Now we need to apply 1914399 next. We need to decide which fragment to apply it to. Likely the remaining aromatic fragment "O=[N+]([O-])c1ccc2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2". Apply 1914399 to that. Let's check matching.
